claims: For every ε>0 and 0≤δ<1, there exists a (0,0)-CCA next-token predictor whose induced autoregressive generative model is not (ε,δ)-CCA, showing CCA does not compose autoregressively unlike differential privacy (Theorem 4.2).

When an ε-CCA next-token predictor induces an ε'-CCA generative model, ε' is lower-bounded by a quantity that can exceed |y|·ε, meaning stricter per-token ε guarantees can yield worse rollout (whole-sequence) CCA guarantees (Theorem 4.3).

Any algorithm solving the α-approximate CCA-Retrofit problem for α<1/2 with only black-box query access requires Ω̃(2^ℓ) oracle queries in the worst case for length-ℓ outputs, establishing exponential query complexity for post-hoc retrofitting (Theorem 5.5, Section 5).

Imposing CCA directly on the underlying next-token predictor does not guarantee that the resulting autoregressive generative model is CCA, as formalized by the composition failure results (Section 4).
